headline: Megan Moroney is nine for nine in the Hot 20's top 10
dek: ‘Medicine’ reaches No. 10, and every song she has charted has now made the top 10.
body: [[Megan Moroney]]'s ‘Medicine’ climbs 11-10 on this week's Hot 20. With that, all nine songs she has charted have reached the top 10. It's a perfect record that only a handful of acts have kept going this long.

The run so far. It started at the top. Her first entry, ‘Tennessee Orange,’ debuted in January 2023 and went all the way to No. 1, and ‘Traitor Joe’ followed it there that summer. ‘I'm Not Pretty’ peaked at No. 5 and ‘No Caller ID’ at No. 8. Then came four straight No. 1s: ‘Mama I Lied,’ ‘Am I Okay,’ ‘6 Months Later’ and ‘Wedding Dress.’ That last one spent seven weeks on top this year, the longest stay at No. 1 of her career.

Six No. 1s from nine songs. Two thirds of everything she has released to the chart has gone to No. 1. ‘Medicine’ is the third charting song from her album Cloud 9, after ‘6 Months Later’ and ‘Wedding Dress.’

The perfect-record club. Moroney joins a short list of acts with at least nine entries that all made the top 10. [[Kip Moore]] leads it by a wide margin: all 21 of his songs have reached the top 10, including ‘Faith in the Wind’ at No. 8 this week. [[George Strait]], [[Leann Rimes]] and [[Lainey Wilson]] are each 13 for 13, [[Chris Young]] is 11 for 11, and [[The Band Perry]] and [[Morgan Wade]] are 10 for 10.

Awards season. The timing doesn't hurt. Moroney goes into this year's Country Awards with five nominations, including her first for Entertainer of the Year, and ‘Wedding Dress’ is up for both Single and Song of the Year.

headline: Who will win at the 2026 Country Awards? Three experts make their picks
dek: The analyst follows the chart, the critic follows the writing, and the fan follows the heart. They don't always agree.
body: The 2026 Country Awards nominations are set, so we asked three very different voices to call the winners. The Analyst goes strictly by the past year on the Hot 20: No. 1s, weeks on top and staying power. The Critic cares about craft, meaning the writing, the singing and whether the record says something. The Fan picks with the heart, the songs that got played the most in the car this year.

Entertainer of the Year. The Analyst picks [[Ella Langley]], and it isn't close on paper. She has four No. 1s and 13 weeks at No. 1 over the past year, the most of any nominee, and she's the reigning winner. The Critic goes with [[Megan Moroney]]: “Cloud 9 is the sound of a writer who knows exactly who she is, and this is her first Entertainer nomination. Reward the leap.” The Fan picks [[Zach Top]]: “Two No. 1s, the most fun shows in country and a sound that makes 1995 feel brand new.”

Female Vocalist. The Analyst and the Fan both pick Langley. The Critic stays with Moroney, pointing to the restraint of ‘Wedding Dress,’ which a quieter singer would have overplayed. Two votes to one for Langley.

Male Vocalist. The Analyst picks Zach Top, whose ‘South of Sanity’ and ‘When You See Me’ spent seven weeks at No. 1 between them. The Critic picks [[David Nail]], whose cover of Bruce Cockburn's ‘Pacing the Cage’ reached No. 2: “It's the best vocal performance on the ballot, full stop.” The Fan picks [[Kip Moore]]: “Twenty-one songs, twenty-one top 10s. He's earned it.”

Vocal Duo/Group. The Analyst picks [[Flatland Cavalry]], the only nominee with a No. 1 this year (‘A Life Where We Work Out’ with Kaitlin Butts). The Critic picks [[Maddie & Tae]]: “Their harmonies are still the gold standard, and they're the most decorated act in the show's history for a reason.” The Fan picks [[The Castellows]], whose ‘Love Is A Game’ is climbing the chart right now.

New Artist. The Analyst picks [[Mackenzie Carpenter]], who has a No. 1 (‘Jesus, I'm Jealous’) and two more top 5 hits this year. The Critic likes Flatland Cavalry's songwriting depth. The Fan picks [[Kevin Powers]], whose ‘Move On’ with Shaboozey made it to No. 1.

Album of the Year. The Analyst picks Langley's Dandelion, which has sent three songs to No. 1 for a combined 12 weeks. The Critic picks Moroney's Cloud 9, which reviewers called her most confident work. The Fan picks Top's Ain't In It For My Health.

Single of the Year. The Analyst picks ‘Wedding Dress,’ whose seven weeks at No. 1 are the most of any song on the ballot. The Critic and the Fan both pick ‘Choosin' Texas,’ which the Fan calls “the song you sing along to with the windows down,” and the Critic calls a classic country record in every sense.

Song of the Year. Here the Analyst and the Critic agree: ‘Wedding Dress.’ For the Critic, it's the writing of the year: a spare, acoustic song about realizing at the altar that you never got over the one who got away. It turns the fairy tale into something unsettling without a wasted line. The Fan goes with ‘Choosin' Texas,’ the story of losing a homesick partner to his Texas hometown and the woman waiting there, told from the long drive back east.

The consensus. Two of three experts land on Ella Langley for Female Vocalist and on ‘Wedding Dress’ for Song of the Year. Everything else is up for grabs, which is exactly how an awards night should feel.

headline: Miranda Lambert was there on day one. Her 34th Hot 20 entry proves she never left
dek: ‘Two Things Can Be True’ debuts at No. 20, putting her one entry behind Carrie Underwood's record.
body: [[Miranda Lambert]]'s ‘Two Things Can Be True’ enters the Hot 20 at No. 20 this week. It's her 34th entry, second only to [[Carrie Underwood]]'s 35. It extends a chart career that began the very first week the Hot 20 existed.

The first chart. When the Hot 20 began on January 28, 2010, Lambert had three songs on it: ‘White Liar’ at No. 3, plus ‘Dead Flowers’ and ‘Gunpowder & Lead.’ A few weeks later ‘The House That Built Me’ jumped from No. 18 to No. 2 in a single week. More than 16 years on, that's still the biggest one-week climb in the chart's history. It reached No. 1 three weeks after that.

The records. Lambert has 11 No. 1s and 28 total weeks at No. 1. ‘Over You’ ruled for nine weeks in 2012, the longest reign the Hot 20 has seen, a record it now shares with Kenny Chesney and Grace Potter's ‘You and Tequila’ and Kip Moore and Morgan Wade's ‘If I Was Your Lover.’ ‘Tin Man’ added eight more weeks in 2017. Her No. 1s span 15 years, from ‘The House That Built Me’ in 2010 to ‘Run’ in 2025.

Good company. She's also one of the chart's great collaborators. ‘We Were Us’ with Keith Urban and ‘Santa Fe’ with Parker McCollum both reached No. 2, and ‘Somethin' Bad’ with Carrie Underwood made No. 5. She even crossed over to the Pop 10, where ‘Drunk’ with Elle King peaked at No. 2 in 2021.

The count. At 34 entries, Lambert trails only Underwood. Her 11 No. 1s tie her with Kip Moore for fifth all-time, behind Underwood (21), Carly Pearce (18), Kenny Chesney (12) and Maddie & Tae (12). Sixteen years after she showed up on the very first chart, her story is still being written.

headline: Ella Langley leads the 2026 Country Awards nominations with six
dek: Megan Moroney, Kacey Musgraves and Zach Top follow with five each.
body: Last year's Entertainer of the Year, [[Ella Langley]], leads the 2026 Country Awards with six nominations: Entertainer, Female Vocalist, Album for Dandelion, Single and Song for “Choosin' Texas”, and Music Video for “Be Her”. She won four awards in 2025, including Entertainer and Female Vocalist.

[[Megan Moroney]], [[Kacey Musgraves]] and [[Zach Top]] have five nominations each, and all three join Langley in both Entertainer and Album. Moroney's “Wedding Dress”, which spent seven weeks at No. 1, is up for Single and Song, and this is her first Entertainer nomination. Musgraves is back in Entertainer for the first time since 2016, with “Loneliest Girl” up for Song. Top won Male Vocalist and New Artist last year and returns in Male Vocalist.

Several acts earn their first nominations. [[Kevin Powers]] leads them with four: Male Vocalist, New Artist, and Single and Musical Event for “Move On” with [[Shaboozey]]. [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] has three (Female Vocalist, New Artist and Album for Hey Country Queen), as does [[Flatland Cavalry]] (Duo/Group, New Artist and Musical Event for “A Life Where We Work Out” with Kaitlin Butts). [[Danielle Bradbery]] picks up two, for Female Vocalist and “Dent” in Single.

The veterans are here too. [[Carly Pearce]], already the most nominated act in the show's history, adds two more for 40 in all, including her eighth Entertainer nomination. [[Maddie & Tae]], the show's biggest winners with 16 awards, return in Duo/Group.

headline: Song of the Year should go to the best writing. Here's where it lives
dek: A critic's read on the 2026 contenders, where the lyric matters as much as the run.
body: Record of the Year rewards how a song sounds and how it landed. Song of the Year is meant to ask a harder question: what is actually on the page? A long run at No. 1 gets a song into the conversation, but the writing should settle it. Nominations aren't final yet, so this is a look at the year's biggest Pop 10 songs through that lens. Last year's nominees, ‘Bite My Tongue’ and ‘Let You Go,’ can't return.

‘Brutalist,’ [[Kim Petras]]. The most daring piece of writing of the year. Petras built it from a childhood memory: long drives across Germany with her architect father to get hormone treatment, him critiquing the concrete buildings they passed. The title does double duty, naming the architecture outside the car window and the hard, load-bearing resolve inside it. The chugging, Kraftwerk-style beat keeps the car moving, so the production serves the story instead of decorating it. It's a pop song about something pop rarely touches, told without a speech.

‘Weather for Tennis,’ [[Hilary Duff]]. The surprise of the year on the page. Duff writes about a relationship where she keeps handing out second chances to someone who keeps breaking promises, then turns the camera on herself, tracing her own avoidance of conflict back to her parents' divorce. That self-implication is what lifts it above a breakup song. The title reads like a forecast for conditions that never quite arrive, which is exactly how the song feels. Written for an album she made with her husband, Matthew Koma, it's the most grown-up writing of her career.

‘Bandaids,’ [[Katy Perry]]. A song carried by one image, and Perry commits to it: quick fixes on a wound too deep for them. The verses stack smaller pictures on top, flowers sent too late, splinters piling up, the slow sense of flatlining while trying to save something. The central metaphor is familiar, and some lines lean on it a little hard. But the closing turn, admitting she'd choose it all again, gives the song a grace her bigger hits rarely needed.

‘Stateside,’ [[Pink Pantheress]] and Zara Larsson. The best-built song in the field. Its subject is small, the first giddy rush of a crush, and it's stitched together from echoes of Adina Howard's ‘Freak Like Me’ and Groove Armada's ‘I See You Baby.’ Larsson's added verse turns it into a conversation across the Atlantic. As writing it's light, and voters may decide it belongs in Record of the Year. As construction it's close to flawless.

‘Cruel World,’ [[Holly Humberstone]]. A long-distance song about how the world itself seems to warp when the person you love isn't in it. Humberstone has always been strongest at small, specific feelings, and the title track of her second album points that skill at something sunnier without losing it.

‘Cranberry,’ [[girlsweetvoiced]]. The quietest writing in the race, and on purpose. It's a whispered, shy confession about everyday romance, the kind of song that works by holding back. Its gift is turning shyness itself into the hook.

The verdict. Plenty of songs had longer runs this year, but the writing narrows the field fast. ‘Brutalist’ and ‘Weather for Tennis’ say the most and say it in ways only their writers could. ‘Bandaids’ is close behind on the strength of its ending. If Song of the Year is about the song, that's where it should be decided.

headline: Kenny Chesney is back in the top two for the first time since 2019
dek: “Silver Sands Marina” holds at No. 2, his best placing in almost seven years.
body: “Silver Sands Marina” holds at No. 2 on the Country Hot 20 this week, its second straight week in the runner-up spot. It is [[Kenny Chesney]]'s first top-two hit since “Tip of My Tongue” spent a week at No. 1 on November 14, 2019, almost seven years ago.
The song took the long road. It debuted at No. 18 on July 23 and spent four weeks at No. 7 before jumping five spots to No. 2 on October 8.
Chesney never went far in between. “Knowing You” in 2021 and “Just to Say We Did” in 2025 both stopped at No. 4. “Silver Sands Marina” is his 29th Hot 20 entry, his 24th top 10 and his 19th top 5.

linkText: Every #1 from the Pop 10's first months
headline: The Pop 10 turns 15
dek: How a high school drive became 15 years, 780 charts and 267 No. 1s.
body: The Pop 10 started the same fall I started driving. Once I had my own car in high school, the radio was on everywhere I went, and it pulled me into pop music in a way nothing had before. I grew to love the genre so much that I gave it a chart of its own. The first Pop 10 arrived on October 27, 2011, and David Guetta and Usher's ‘Without You’ was its first No. 1.

Before the Pop 10. Pop wasn't new to Willboard. During the transitional era, from January 2010 to October 2011, pop songs competed with country on the Hot 20. Shakira took ‘Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)’ all the way to No. 1 in 2010, and [[Demi Lovato]] did the same with ‘Skyscraper’ in 2011. [[Lady Gaga]] placed seven songs on the Hot 20, led by ‘Alejandro’ at No. 3.

The radio years (2011 to 2013). Dev's ‘In The Dark’ finished as the first Year-End No. 1. Then came the record that still stands: Gotye and Kimbra's ‘Somebody That I Used To Know’ spent 15 weeks at No. 1 in 2012 and 36 weeks on the chart. Bruno Mars followed with 11 weeks on top for ‘Locked Out of Heaven.’ In December 2013 the chart moved from feel to Spotify playlists.

The mid-2010s. [[Ariana Grande]] and Iggy Azalea's ‘Problem’ ruled 2014 with 10 weeks at No. 1. In 2015 [[Meghan Trainor]] arrived in a big way, taking the top two spots on the Year-End chart with ‘Like I'm Gonna Lose You’ and ‘Dear Future Husband.’ [[The Chainsmokers]] owned 2016 with nine weeks on top for ‘Don't Let Me Down,’ the start of a run that has made them the chart's second-longest leaders.

Counting the plays (2017 to now). Since December 2017 the Pop 10 has run on real play counts, first from Last.fm and since 2023 from stats.fm. Demi Lovato came full circle with ‘Sorry Not Sorry,’ the 2017 Year-End No. 1. Sam Smith topped the year twice, with ‘How Do You Sleep’ in 2019 and ‘Unholy’ with Kim Petras in 2022. In 2023 [[Cassandra Coleman]]'s ‘Habit’ came within one week of Gotye's record with 14 weeks at No. 1. And the chart has gone global: Erika Vikman's ‘Ich Komme’ led for seven weeks in 2025, the same year the Pop Awards added Foreign Language Song of the Year.

Milestones. The 100th song to reach No. 1 was Mariah Carey and YG's ‘I Don't’ on March 2, 2017. Meghan Trainor fittingly brought up No. 1 number 200 with ‘Made You Look’ on December 1, 2022, and Chloe Tang and Casandra's ‘Running on Blue’ became the 250th last December. Panic! At the Disco's ‘High Hopes’ was the 500th song ever to chart, in November 2018. The 1,000th was [[Hilary Duff]]'s ‘Weather for Tennis,’ which debuted at No. 1 on March 5 of this year and was still on top a week later for the 750th Pop 10.

By the numbers. Through 780 charts, 267 different songs have reached No. 1. Meghan Trainor owns the record books with 13 No. 1s and 42 weeks on top, ahead of The Chainsmokers (34 weeks) and Ariana Grande (32). Here's to the next 15.

linkText: Dolly Parton's full Willboard chart history
headline: Dolly Parton's Willboard legacy: six hits, two charts, and records that still stand
dek: Two months after her death at 80, a look back at her years on the Hot 20 and the Pop 10.
body: [[Dolly Parton]] died on August 25 in Nashville at 80, and on Wednesday night the CMA's two-hour tribute brought country's biggest names together to sing her songs. Her catalog is far older than Willboard, but she found her way onto these charts six times over 13 years, and some of what she did here hasn't been matched.

Where it started. Her first appearance came in the chart's opening weeks. During the transitional era, ‘Jolene’ debuted at No. 14 on March 18, 2010, and climbed to No. 8 the next week, more than 35 years after its release. Its four-week run was the first sign that her songs don't belong to any one decade.

‘Home’ (2014). Her signature Willboard moment took patience. ‘Home’ debuted at No. 17 on July 10, 2014, and spent 14 weeks climbing before it reached No. 1 on October 9. It held the top spot for two weeks, spent 18 weeks on the chart and finished No. 14 on the 2014 Year-End chart. She was 68, and 12 years later she is still the oldest woman to top the Hot 20. The song also earned her a Music Video of the Year nomination at the 2015 Country Awards.

‘Pure and Simple’ (2016). The title track of her 2016 album entered at No. 20 on August 4 and made a slow, steady climb to No. 4, where it stayed for three weeks. Its 20-week run is her longest on any Willboard chart.

Crossing over (2019). Few country legends have topped the Pop 10, and Parton did it at 73. Galantis' ‘Faith,’ with Mr. Probz, debuted at No. 6 on November 28, 2019, and reached No. 1 two weeks later. It led for four straight weeks, carrying her into 2020, and finished No. 24 on the 2019 Pop Year-End chart. At the time she was the oldest act ever to top the Pop 10. Only Elton John and Cher have since topped it older, and Cher is the only woman to do it.

Still collaborating. She kept showing up alongside younger acts. ‘Happy All the Time’ with Sam Williams, Hank Williams' grandson, reached No. 12 on the Hot 20 in 2021, and ‘Bets On Us’ with Cheat Codes climbed to No. 5 on the Pop 10 in January 2023, her last Willboard hit.

By the numbers. Six chart entries, 65 weeks on the charts and six weeks at No. 1. She is one of only seven acts to send a song to No. 1 on both the Hot 20 and the Pop 10. Her legacy is much bigger than any chart, but on this one she left a mark that will be hard to touch.
